§6Low-Density Element§f

§aLightweight aerospace panels forged with stellar flux. Rockets eat these by the stack.§f

Low-Density Elements are welded in the arc welder from PVC or hard plastic bars, fiberglass, and aluminium or titanium plates. They need §e5-10 kHE/t§f power and take 10 seconds each.

§6Primary use§f: Each §bSoyuz-FG§f rocket needs §e32§f of them. Orbital modules need 1 each. Satellite bases use 8. Since you'll be launching multiple Soyuz rockets for Gerald and satellites, you'll burn through stacks fast.

The recipe is straightforward but the volume adds up. A single Gerald launch cycle (rocket + orbital module) costs 33 low-density elements. Factor in satellite launches and you're looking at 50+ per run.

§ePS:§f Automate the arc welder with an assembler pipeline. Keep titanium and fiberglass stocked. These components gate your entire space program.
